name: Sgt. Chapman
role: Sergeant (E7), in charge of the van, Larry thinks
summary: Photographed shirtless beside Larry in VN-0024, an older, powerfully built man with a graying crew cut: "Sargent Chapman, he was a rank E7 and Me on the right." Asked on 2026-09-13 what Chapman did, Larry said: "He was kind of in charge of the van and kind of in charge of scheduling, who would work what. Most of the guys didn't like going to the mountain at all. Chapman would ask who wanted to go to the mountain." Asked about an officer in charge of the van: "I don't think we had one. I think Sargeant Chapman was in charge of it. I never seen officers in there." His son, who typed the call, adds that Larry seemed unsure who ran the van and may have been giving his best guess. Larry thinks the night-time picture of him in the van (VN-0015) was "taken at nighttime by Weaver or Chapman."
researchNotes: Resolved 2026-08-23 (giscus-vn-0024-c18119894, paraphrase): Larry did not know Chapman in basic training, "No one from basic training was in Vietnam with him", repeated in his son's report of 2026-09-13 (2026-09-13-son-no-one-from-training.json). An earlier phone-call note had put the name in a basic-training context; that was a mis-link, and it was removed from the summary on 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md. Chapman is an in-country man only, an E7 in Larry's telling. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0015-c18415735): a hedged placement with Larry in the van. 2026-09-13 (2026-09-13-phone-chapman.json and -van-officer.json, transcribed, by telephone): the van and scheduling, and the mountain postings going to volunteers. An E7's name is a good morning-report target once the unit is settled. 2026-09-15, on his son's decision (no spelling notes on public pages): the rendered aliases were trimmed; removed from display, kept here: "Sgt. "Chapman"".
